_note: pp_client_sheet.py: short client-facing sheet. 'automations' = the ones planned to turn on (event = what starts it, in plain words, used as 'Right after …' / '1 day after …'). 'off' = built but kept off (one line each). 'yours' = the client's own automations already running. Branch labels: '' = no condition text; null = path is not shown.
title: Your automations, in plain English
subtitle: What your customers receive, when, and in what words. Tick a box next to each message and send it back.

journey.title: A new lead reaches you
journey.text: Call, text, web chat or your quote form: Nathan gets an alert and the lead gets a card on your lead board.

journey.title: You miss their call
journey.text: They get a text right away, and one reminder 30 minutes later if they don't answer.

journey.title: The lead goes quiet
journey.text: Move the card to “No Response”: 3 friendly texts go out over about a week.

journey.title: You send a quote
journey.text: Move the card to “Quote Sent”: 2 follow-up texts if they don't reply.

journey.title: They miss an appointment
journey.text: Move the card to “No Show”: 2 texts to reschedule.

journey.title: They sign up
journey.text: Move the card to “Won”: they're tagged as a customer and welcomed.

journey.title: A few weeks later
journey.text: We ask how we did. 4–5 stars get your Google review link; 1–3 stars alert Nathan first.

journey.title: Lost leads and old customers
journey.text: Lost leads get a feedback email and a 90-day check-in. Win-back messages go out only when you start a campaign.

journey_tip: Most messages start when a card moves on your lead board. If a card is never moved, nothing is sent: your team stays in control.

notes.SMS 1: Your phone system already sends its own missed-call text (see “Already running”). Only one of the two should go out: see question 2.

No Response Follow-up.event: you move the card to “No Response”
No Response Follow-up.after_last: No reply after the third text: the card moves to Lost.

Quote Sent Follow-up.event: you move the card to “Quote Sent”
Quote Sent Follow-up.after_last: No reply after the second text: the card moves to Lost.

No-Show Follow-up.event: you move the card to “No Show”

notes.Welcome Email: Your agreement automation already sends a welcome email and text to new customers. See question 3.
notes.SMS: Your agreement automation already sends a welcome text from Nathan. See question 3.

notes.SMS - Request NPS Feedback: Right now only weekly customers get this. I'll make repair and construction customers get it too (question 5).

Review Response - Positive.event: they leave a 4 or 5-star Google review

Review Response - Negative.event: they leave a Google review of 3 stars or less

Reactivation Campaign - SMS.group: Win-back campaign (only when you start one)

Reactivation Campaign - Email.group: Win-back campaign (only when you start one)

decisions.q: Can I tag your current customers (the ones from QuickBooks, Skimmer and the agreement emails) as “existing customer”?
decisions.why: Then a call or text from a current customer never gets lead texts or a “new lead” card. Needed before anything is turned on.

decisions.q: Missed-call text: keep yours, or use M1 + its 30-minute reminder (M2)?
decisions.why: Both are on today's plan; only one should go out. I can also put your wording into M1.
decisions.default: Your wording in M1, plus M2

decisions.q: New weekly customers: keep only your welcome (agreement email + Nathan's text), without M{won_first}–M{won_last}?
decisions.why: Otherwise a new customer gets two welcome emails and two welcome texts.

decisions.q: Should leads from your website quote form also get a card on the lead board (and the follow-ups)?
decisions.why: Nathan keeps getting his text alert, just once.

decisions.q: Ask repair / install and construction customers for a rating too (about 3 and 8 weeks after the job)?
decisions.why: Today only weekly customers would be asked.

decisions.q: Are you running Google Ads (or planning to)?
decisions.why: If yes, I'll connect your ad tracking number and form; if not, those stay off.
